assumptions.text: Answers connect N1 and code N1: contracts cover only the messages that leave the horch process or have a human, an agent or an external system on 1 end: the command channel, the file protocol and the external facts. The 21 in-process messages get no wire schema; contracts.md lists them for code-level tests.

Answers code N2: every entry id equals its connect message id, so the code.json tests 'contract: <id>' and 'idempotent: <id>' bind to these entries. Each semantics line keeps the connect idempotency key as written.

write-result and submit-plan use the field names of the design examples of result.json and plan.yaml (task, attempt, files_changed, base_branch), not the connect payload names (taskId, attemptId), because the design wins over a later artifact and the ticket says to keep the design names. Decision D1 records the call for the files that the design gives no example for.
Every other entry keeps the connect payload names in camelCase as an interim, until the operator decides D1.
Id formats come from the comments of the design ledger schema: I-0007, F-0003, T-0007-02, T-0007-02/A1 or I-0007/clarifying/1, T-0007-02/A1/Q1, refs/horch/rescue/T-0007-03/1, fleet/I-0007/T-0007-03.

A Markdown file of the file protocol (assumptions.md, spec.md) is carried as 1 string field with the whole file content; requirements.yaml and plan.yaml are carried as objects with the design field names.

answer-question carries the answer as an object {case, text}. case is the closed list of ledger questions.answer_case (covered, revise, replan, own_decision). connect writes 'answer|assumption'; an own_decision answer is the assumption case.
replan-task carries planChange as 1 task in the plan.yaml task shape, with the same key.
result.json requires task, attempt, status, summary and commits; files_changed, acceptance_self_check and notes_for_next are optional. commits may be empty.
attempt-exited exitStatus is the integer exit code, or null when a signal ended the process (ledger attempts.exit_code is nullable).
approve-assumptions answers approved false for a refusal (stale hash, or idea not in awaiting_approval). The reply carries no reason field because connect lists none.
The request of trial-merge-result names the other side as a feature id or the literal 'primary' for the primary branch.
task.kind and task-escalated.reason stay open strings: the design names known values but no closed list.

open_questions.text: task.yaml, inbox/START.md, heartbeat.json, verdict.json, plan.verdict.json and approval.json cross a process boundary between fleetd, the wrapper and agents, but connect has no message for them, so this step has no contract for them. Should ddd-connect add a message for each? The design gives examples of task.yaml and heartbeat.json, and protocol rule 4 needs a schema for every file type.

add-idea and add-direct-idea have no idempotency key, but their request-file channel is at-least-once. A request file ingested twice creates 2 ideas. Should the request carry a request id that fleetd de-duplicates on?
result.json status: the design shows only 'completed'. Which other values may a worker write (for example blocked, partial), and is the list closed?

connect payload names differ from the design file field names (taskId and attemptId against task and attempt). Should ddd-connect adopt the design names, so that a prefill re-run does not add the connect names back to write-result?
approve-assumptions replies only approved. Should the reply carry the refusal reason (stale hash, wrong state, caller inside a fleet attempt)?
usage-limit-reported requires resetAt. A provider outage can have no known reset time. Should resetAt be optional, and what does fleetd wait for then?

entries.name: Add Idea
entries.description: The operator captures an idea from any terminal; fleetd records it as captured, and the dispatcher starts its sub-orchestrator on the next pass.
semantics: Each accepted request creates exactly 1 immutable idea.md and 1 ledger row in state captured, and the reply carries its new ideaId.
No idempotency key exists: a request file that is ingested twice creates 2 ideas (open question Q2).
Only fleetd writes the ledger. When fleetd is down, horch writes a request file and fleetd reads it at start, so the reply arrives only on the sync channel.
entries.termsOfUse: Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed, renamed or retyped field is 2.0. The horch CLI and fleetd ship in 1 binary, so the operator never meets a version skew, but a request file written by an older horch and read at start must still validate.

channels.note: request file under the state root when fleetd is down; fleetd reads it at start

entries.name: Add Direct Idea
entries.description: The operator adds a ticket they wrote; the ticket stands for their approval, so the idea skips research, the interview and the assumptions phase and goes to ticketing.
semantics: The command is refused when the caller's process tree contains a recorded fleet attempt, like horch idea approve.
Without featureId, fleetd creates a new feature whose branch name is the kebab-case ticket title with a number suffix when the name exists, and returns its featureId.
fleetd writes the ledger row before it creates the branch. A plan that plan validation refuses sends the idea to needs-you/ with the reason.
No idempotency key exists: a request file that is ingested twice creates 2 ideas (open question Q2).

entries.name: Approve Assumptions
entries.description: The operator approves the assumptions of an idea; this licenses the sub-orchestrator to write the spec, and no spec or task exists for the idea before it.
semantics: An approval of the same assumptionsHash is a no-op that answers approved true again; a stale hash is refused with approved false.
fleetd writes approval.json itself with the hash the operator saw and ignores an approval.json written by any other process (FR-10, I7).
The command is refused when the caller's process tree contains a recorded fleet attempt, and agent profiles deny it.

entries.name: Abandon Task Branch
entries.description: The operator abandons an escalated task branch; its work survives on a rescue ref, and the branch leaves the landing queue for good.
semantics: Only the operator abandons a task branch; abandoned is terminal.
The branch is dropped only after its rescue ref exists and is verified (I10, CC7); the reply always names that ref.
An abandoned branch is not abandoned twice: a repeat returns the same rescueRef and changes nothing.

entries.name: Write Assumptions
entries.description: The sub-orchestrator ends clarifying with assumptions.md; a valid file opens the feature on first write and asks the operator for approval.
semantics: fleetd ingests the file once per (path, content hash); the file is written atomically and never edited after it lands.
A file with any item marked [open] is refused; a valid file moves the idea to awaiting_approval and triggers approval-requested.
The [assumed] items are exactly what the operator approves; a revise sends the idea back to clarifying and needs a new file.
entries.termsOfUse: Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed, renamed or retyped field is 2.0. fleetd rejects a file or request that fails this schema (design protocol rule 4), so a 2.0 ships together with the matching horch, fleet helper and prompt changes.

entries.name: Write Spec
entries.description: The sub-orchestrator writes the spec and the numbered requirements of an approved idea; valid files move the idea to ticketing.
semantics: fleetd ingests the pair once per (ideaId, content hash); both files are written atomically.
fleetd accepts the files only while the idea holds an approval.json whose hash matches the current assumptions.md (FR-10).
Every requirement cites an approved assumption or one of the operator's answers; a requirement without a citation fails validation.
entries.termsOfUse: Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed, renamed or retyped field is 2.0. fleetd rejects a file or request that fails this schema (design protocol rule 4), so a 2.0 ships together with the matching horch, fleet helper and prompt changes.

entries.name: Submit Plan
entries.description: The sub-orchestrator submits the plan of an idea; a plan that passes validation commits all its tasks in 1 transaction and the idea goes to in_progress.
semantics: fleetd ingests the plan once per (ideaId, plan content hash); plan.verdict.json records the result of each ingest.
A plan commits all-or-nothing, only after schema, DAG, coverage, profile and citation checks pass; every requirement must be covered by at least 1 task (I3).
A plan is refused when the project declares no fast gate and full gate, or when a judgment-kind task has no paired judge task in another session.
Only a committed plan creates tasks; no AI creates a task any other way (FM-1).
entries.termsOfUse: Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed, renamed or retyped field is 2.0. fleetd rejects a file or request that fails this schema (design protocol rule 4), so a 2.0 ships together with the matching horch, fleet helper and prompt changes.

entries.name: Answer Question
entries.description: The sub-orchestrator answers a worker question; an answer lets fleetd resume the parked task with it.
semantics: fleetd records 1 answer per questionId; a second answer for the same questionId is refused.
A covered answer must carry a citation, and fleetd checks that the cited line exists.
A revise answer goes to the operator and pauses only the affected tasks; an own_decision answer is recorded as an assumption the operator can reverse.
The answer goes to the decision log of the feature and to every later task of the feature.
entries.termsOfUse: Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed, renamed or retyped field is 2.0. fleetd rejects a file or request that fails this schema (design protocol rule 4), so a 2.0 ships together with the matching horch, fleet helper and prompt changes.

entries.name: Replan Task
entries.description: The sub-orchestrator replans a task that task-execution gave back; the replanned task returns to task-execution.
semantics: fleetd accepts 1 replan per task: once per (taskId, replan round). A task that fails after its replan goes to needs-you/.
The replanned task passes the same plan checks as a plan; coverage of the idea's requirements must still hold (I3).
entries.termsOfUse: Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed, renamed or retyped field is 2.0. fleetd rejects a file or request that fails this schema (design protocol rule 4), so a 2.0 ships together with the matching horch, fleet helper and prompt changes.

entries.name: Write Result
entries.description: The worker claims its attempt is finished; the claim licenses fleetd to run the verifier, and only the verifier moves the task to done.
semantics: 1 result per attempt: result.json is written atomically and never rewritten; fleetd ingests it once per (task, attempt).
The result is a claim, not a fact: a task is done only when result.json validates and the verifier's check passes in the worker sandbox (RR-3, SR-4).
acceptance_self_check is advisory; the verifier never trusts it.
A process that exits with commits and no result gets 1 short resume of the same session to write it; an exit without a valid result is outcome no_result.
entries.termsOfUse: Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed, renamed or retyped field is 2.0. fleetd rejects a file or request that fails this schema (design protocol rule 4), so a 2.0 ships together with the matching horch, fleet helper and prompt changes.

entries.name: Ask Question
entries.description: A worker asks a blocking question; the worker commits its work in progress and exits, and its task parks with no process until the answer arrives.
semantics: 1 file per questionId; fleetd ingests each file once and creates 1 ledger question row owned by the sub-orchestrator of the feature.
The worker exits after it writes the file; the other tasks of the feature go on.
Past the question's time limit, fleetd escalates it to needs-you/ with a herdr notification (RR-12).
entries.termsOfUse: Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed, renamed or retyped field is 2.0. fleetd rejects a file or request that fails this schema (design protocol rule 4), so a 2.0 ships together with the matching horch, fleet helper and prompt changes.

entries.name: Attempt Exited
entries.description: The agent process of an attempt has exited; the fact lets fleetd end the attempt and decide its outcome.
semantics: Once per attemptId: exit.json is immutable, and a second ingest is a no-op.
The wrapper reports facts and decides nothing; fleetd decides the outcome (no_result when hasResult is false and the repair resume fails).
entries.termsOfUse: The agent CLI owns the wire fact; this schema is our view of it at the ACL boundary. Changes in The agent CLI land in the fleet-run wrapper; nothing else reads The agent CLI directly. Additive changes only within version 1.x.

entries.name: Usage Limit Reported
entries.description: A worker's provider pool hit a usage limit or an outage; the attempt is not stuck and burns no attempt.
semantics: Once per (attemptId, pool); a repeat for an attempt that already moved to its fallback is ignored.
Never a stall: fleetd restarts the task at once on the fallback persona when it is on another provider, else the task waits in waiting_quota with its lease paused until resetAt (RR-11).
entries.termsOfUse: The provider owns the wire fact; this schema is our view of it at the ACL boundary. Changes in The provider land in the worker-profiles adapter of that CLI; nothing else reads The provider directly. Additive changes only within version 1.x.

entries.name: Primary Branch Moved
entries.description: The primary branch has a new tip; feature branches rebase, bottom of a stack first, and trial merges run again.
semantics: Once per (primaryBranch, tip); a second report of the same tip is a no-op.
Each feature branch rebases and its fast gate runs again; a full gate pass judged on the old tip goes stale.
entries.termsOfUse: git owns the wire fact; this schema is our view of it at the ACL boundary. Changes in git land in the integration git adapter; nothing else reads git directly. Additive changes only within version 1.x.

entries.name: Trial Merge Result
entries.description: git answers whether 2 tips merge cleanly, with no checkout; a conflict stacks the younger feature on the older one and opens 1 resolver task.
semantics: Advisory and safe to repeat: git merge-tree --write-tree changes no branch and no worktree; the result is a ledger fact keyed by (left tip, right tip).
The answer is valid only for the 2 tips it judged; a move of either tip needs a new trial merge.
The call runs outside the ledger write transaction and has a 3 min wall-clock bound with no retry (04 F11, CC6).
entries.termsOfUse: git owns the wire fact; this schema is our view of it at the ACL boundary. Changes in git land in the integration git adapter; nothing else reads git directly. Additive changes only within version 1.x.

entries.name: Check Merged
entries.description: The clock asks integration whether a feature's changes are in the primary branch; a yes moves the feature to merged.
semantics: Level-triggered and safe to repeat: feature-merged is emitted once per featureId.
Merged is read from git by content, also after a squash merge, never from the GitHub API (I8).
entries.termsOfUse: The clock owns the wire fact; this schema is our view of it at the ACL boundary. Changes in The clock land in the fleetd pass loop; nothing else reads The clock directly. Additive changes only within version 1.x.

entries.name: Apply Stall Ladder
entries.description: The clock asks task-execution to move a quiet attempt 1 rung down the stall ladder: doorbell, doorbell again, then end the attempt as stalled.
semantics: Each rung is recorded once per (attemptId, rung); a repeat of the same rung does nothing.
Time counts only while the machine is awake; a sleep never moves a rung (PL-4).
A usage limit is never a stall: an attempt in waiting_quota gets no rung.
entries.termsOfUse: The clock owns the wire fact; this schema is our view of it at the ACL boundary. Changes in The clock land in the fleetd pass loop; nothing else reads The clock directly. Additive changes only within version 1.x.

entries.name: Approval Requested
entries.description: fleetd asks the operator to approve an idea's assumptions; until the operator approves or revises, the idea's lease is paused.
semantics: 1 needs-you/ file per (ideaId, assumptionsHash), plus a herdr notification; a revised assumptions.md gets a new file.
Waiting is not a stall: 1 reminder an hour during working hours, and after 7 days with no answer the idea goes to parked with a note in needs-you/.

entries.name: Worker Question Asked
entries.description: fleetd hands a worker's question to the sub-orchestrator of its feature, which owns the answer.
semantics: 1 inbox file per questionId; delivery repeats on each pass, and fleetd starts the owner when it is not running, until an answer is recorded.
A sub-orchestrator sees only the questions of its own feature (FM-16).

entries.name: Task Escalated
entries.description: A task needs the operator; its task branch stops landing and stays listed for a decision until the operator requeues or abandons it.
semantics: The reconcile pass is level-triggered, so the reaction can run again: 1 needs-you/ file per (taskId, reason), and integration records it once per taskId.
Nothing is removed on escalation: the worktree and branch stay, and only the operator abandons the branch.
An operator requeue of the task resets its attempt count (attempt_floor, 04 L8).

channels.note: integration reads the escalation in the reconcile pass of the same horch process; the pass is level-triggered, so integration records it once per taskId

entries.name: Pull Request Opened
entries.description: A feature passed its full gate on the current primary branch and its pull request is open; the operator may merge it.
semantics: 1 pull request per featureId; a repeat of the reaction returns the same prUrl.
A stacked feature's pull request has the lower feature's branch as its base.
The operator merges by default; fleetd reads merged from git, not from this URL.

decisions.question: Which field-name convention do the file and command-channel payloads use when the design gives no example of the file?

options.summary: Keep the connect payload names in camelCase (taskId, ideaId) for every file without a design example.
pros: Matches connect and code.json as written (code N2)
cons: 2 conventions on 1 wire: result.json uses task and files_changed, other files use taskId
risks: A worker prompt or the fleet helper mixes the 2 conventions and fleetd rejects the file

options.summary: Use the design convention everywhere: snake_case and short id names (task, attempt, idea, feature), as in result.json, task.yaml, plan.yaml and heartbeat.json.
pros: 1 convention on the whole file protocol
Matches every file example in the design
cons: Renames connect payload names; connect and code.json need a re-run to match
risks: A prefill re-run before connect adopts the names adds the camelCase names back

options.summary: Use camelCase everywhere, and rename the design example fields too (taskId, filesChanged).
risks: The implementation follows the design and drifts from the contracts

decisions.rationale: Recommendation: B. The design is approved and every file example in it uses snake_case and short id names, so 1 convention on the wire follows the design. Strongest argument against: connect and code.json then need a re-run to match, and until then the chain carries 2 vocabularies. The step keeps A as an interim for files without a design example (assumption A4) and leaves the call to the operator.
would_flip_if: The operator wants the wire names to match the Rust field names and those are camelCase through serde
The design gains an example that uses camelCase
ddd-connect is not re-run before implementation

plain_words.what: This step wrote 21 contracts: the exact shape of each file or request that crosses a process line in fleetd. These are operator commands, files the sub-orchestrators and workers write, files fleetd writes for them, and facts from git, the agent CLI, the provider and the clock. Each contract has a schema, a good example and bad examples it must reject.
plain_words.decided: The 21 messages that stay inside the 1 horch binary get no contract, only code tests. result.json and plan.yaml keep the field names of the design examples.
plain_words.assumed: The other files keep the connect names (taskId, ideaId) for now. The operator decides the single naming style at the review (decision D1).
plain_words.riskiest: task.yaml, heartbeat.json and verdict.json have no contract, because connect lists no message for them (Q1). A worker or the wrapper built from this catalogue alone would miss them.
